spec.title: Network Observability - Global WAN and Federation Maps
spec.description: Geographic and logical maps of the global network's topology federation: hub, regional spokes and the enterprise DC, coloured by spoke liveness, push age and rejected graph updates.

panels.title: Global WAN - hub to spoke push paths
panels.description: Site locations: global hub London, dc-amer Ashburn, dc-apac Singapore, dc-emea Frankfurt, dc-edge-1 Dublin, dc-edge-2 Amsterdam, EMEA edge spoke exporter (emea-edge1) Paris, enterprise DC hq-dc1 Chicago (standalone discovery, not federated, so it has no push path). Each path is a federation push path from a spoke to the hub, drawn as a curve between sites, not a measured route or circuit. Colour is seconds since the hub last accepted a push (green under 120 s, yellow 120 s, orange 180 s, red 300 s and above). The hub to spoke half is held at 300 s or more (red) whenever network_topology_federation_spoke_up is 0, so a spoke the hub marks down always shows red; the spoke to hub half is the raw push age from network_topology_federation_spoke_last_push_timestamp_seconds. The emea-edge1 path uses the spoke-side network_topology_federation_spoke_push_last_success_unix for both halves. No bandwidth or utilisation is shown: the topology exporters do not measure link traffic.

targets.expr: sum by (src, dst) (label_replace(label_replace((((time() - network_topology_federation_spoke_last_push_timestamp_seconds{job="integrations/network-topology-exporter",instance="netobs-glb-hub:9100"}) and on (spoke_id) (network_topology_federation_spoke_up{job="integrations/network-topology-exporter",instance="netobs-glb-hub:9100"} == 1)) or (clamp_min((time() - network_topology_federation_spoke_last_push_timestamp_seconds{job="integrations/network-topology-exporter",instance="netobs-glb-hub:9100"}), 300) and on (spoke_id) (network_topology_federation_spoke_up{job="integrations/network-topology-exporter",instance="netobs-glb-hub:9100"} == 0))), "src", "hub", "instance", ".*"), "dst", "$1", "spoke_id", "(.+)") or label_replace(label_replace(time() - network_topology_federation_spoke_push_last_success_unix{job="integrations/network-topology-exporter",instance="netobs-spoke-emea:9100"}, "src", "hub", "instance", ".*"), "dst", "emea-edge1", "instance", ".*"))

panels.title: Federation weathermap - push age, liveness and rejected updates
panels.description: Logical hub-and-spoke view of the federated topology estate. Spoke links (A side, spoke to hub) show seconds since the hub last accepted that spoke's push (network_topology_federation_spoke_last_push_timestamp_seconds); colour and width scale against a 300 s staleness budget set on this map (40% yellow, 60% orange, 100% red). A spoke link blinks red when network_topology_federation_spoke_up is 0. The emea-edge1 link uses the spoke-side push_last_success_unix. The validator link shows graph updates rejected by the hub in the last 15 minutes (network_topology_graph_updates_rejected_total, all reasons) against a budget of 20. Node borders: spoke liveness, and network_topology_graph_stale for the hub and the standalone enterprise DC. No bandwidth is shown; the exporters do not measure link traffic.

panels.title: Push age per spoke
panels.description: Seconds since each spoke last pushed to the hub (network_topology_federation_spoke_last_push_timestamp_seconds), plus the emea-edge1 exporter's own last-success age. Scale 0 to 300 s.

panels.title: Rejected graph updates by reason
panels.description: Graph updates the hub rejected, by reason (network_topology_graph_updates_rejected_total, increase per interval). stale_generation means a spoke pushed a graph older than the one the hub already holds.

panels.title: Spoke liveness
panels.description: Liveness of each spoke as tracked by the hub (network_topology_federation_spoke_up: 1 up, 0 down).

panels.title: Push age over time
panels.description: Seconds since last push per spoke; dashed lines mark the 120 s, 180 s and 300 s bands used on the maps.

panels.title: Boundary observations at the hub
panels.description: One row per inter-domain boundary adjacency the hub can see (network_topology_boundary_observation_info): the two peers, the device that reported it, its port and the discovery protocol.

panels.title: Boundary observations by leaf
panels.description: Boundary adjacencies grouped by the leaf the reporting host hangs off (leaf parsed from reporting_device, for example host-leaf01-02 is on leaf-01).

options.content:
### Reading this board

**Global hub** `netobs-glb-hub` (London) federates five regional spokes: dc-amer (Ashburn), dc-apac (Singapore), dc-emea (Frankfurt), dc-edge-1 (Dublin) and dc-edge-2 (Amsterdam). The **emea-edge1** spoke exporter (Paris) reports its own push health. The **enterprise DC** hq-dc1 (Chicago) runs standalone discovery and is not federated.

- Map paths are logical push paths drawn between sites, not circuits.
- Link colour = seconds since last push; red means stale (300 s or more) or marked down by the hub.
- Rejected updates are hub-wide; the exporter does not attribute them to a spoke.
- No link bandwidth is shown anywhere on this board: topology discovery does not measure traffic.

panels.title: Probe agent locations - success and latency
panels.description: One marker per probe location, placed from the sm_check_info geohash label. Colour is mean probe_success across the checks run from that location (green 99% and above, orange 90%, red below), size scales with the number of checks, and the tooltip adds mean probe_duration_seconds. All probe agents currently report the same location geohash, so they share one marker; the table alongside breaks them out per agent.

targets.expr: avg by (geohash) (probe_success * on (instance, job, probe) group_left (region, geohash) max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info))
avg by (geohash) (probe_duration_seconds * on (instance, job, probe) group_left (region, geohash) max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info))
count by (geohash) (max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info))

panels.title: Probe agents - success and latency
panels.description: Per probe agent: region, number of checks (sm_check_info), mean probe_success and mean probe_duration_seconds across its checks.

targets.expr: label_replace(avg by (probe, region) (probe_success * on (instance, job, probe) group_left (region) max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info)), "probe", "$1", "probe", "[^-]+-(private.*)")

label_replace(avg by (probe, region) (probe_duration_seconds * on (instance, job, probe) group_left (region) max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info)), "probe", "$1", "probe", "[^-]+-(private.*)")
label_replace(count by (probe, region) (max by (instance, job, probe, region, geohash) (sm_check_info)), "probe", "$1", "probe", "[^-]+-(private.*)")

panels.title: Probe latency by check
panels.description: probe_duration_seconds per check (job) and probe agent.
